newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Danubius firms, Egis plummets on mixed Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Danubius firms, Egis plummets on mixed Budapest.

text.p: Shares in hotel firm Danubius outperformed, while stocks in pharmaceuticals company Egis underperformed most other papers on the Budapest bourse where shares traded mixed with slightly positive tone.
Danubius shares opened at 5,600 forints, above Monday's close of 5,415 and jumped to a daily high of 5,750 forints in early trade. At 1112 GMT Danubius traded at 5,580 forints, up three percent.
"The share fell to levels (in the past few days) which triggered new purchases, mainly from domestic clients," one trader said.
Another trader said Danubius's price rose on the back of speculative purchases by domestic small investors.
Although Danubius rose above 5,700 forints in early trade, its rise was seen limited as sellers appeared at around 5,600, traders said.
On the negative territory, Egis dropped nearly five percent on foreigners' sales. Egis opened at 11,000 forints, below Monday's close of 11,350 and at 1118 GMT it traded at 10,800 forints, down 550.

Traders said they were not aware of any fresh developments around Egis, but last Thursday afternoon ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett published a 'sell' recommendation on the stock, triggered by the 1996 preliminary results.
Both stocks have had a volume of only a few thousands of shares by 1125 GMT.
